arxiv-2001-00767.title: A Proximal Linearization-based Decentralized Method for Nonconvex Problems with Nonlinear Constraints
arxiv-2001-00767.creator: Yu Yang, Guoqiang Hu, and Costas J. Spanos
arxiv-2001-00767.description: Abstract Decentralized optimization for non-convex problems are now demanding by many emerging applications (e.g., smart grids, smart building, etc.). Though dramatic progress has been achieved in convex problems, the results for non-convex cases, especially with non-linear constraints, are still largely unexplored.

arxiv-2011-04306.title: Ordinal Intensity-Efficient Allocations
arxiv-2011-04306.creator: Georgios Gerasimou
arxiv-2011-04306.description: Abstract We study the assignment problem in situations where, in addition to having ordinal preferences, agents also have ordinal intensities : they can make simple and internally consistent comparisons such as “I prefer a a to b b more than I prefer c c to d d ” without necessarily being able to quantify them.

arxiv-2105-04506.creator: Zhaopin Chen 1 and Boris A. Malomed 1,2

arxiv-2203-13349.title: Occluded Human Mesh Recovery
arxiv-2203-13349.creator: Rawal Khirodkar Shashank Tripathi Kris Kitani
arxiv-2203-13349.description: Abstract Top-down methods for monocular human mesh recovery have two stages: (1) detect human bounding boxes; (2) treat each bounding box as an independent single-human mesh recovery task. Unfortunately, the single-human assumption does not hold in images with multi-human occlusion and crowding. Consequently, top-down methods have difficulties in recovering accurate 3D human meshes under severe person-person occlusion.

arxiv-2205-08361.title: Dynamics of flexible filaments in oscillatory shear flows
arxiv-2205-08361.creator: Francesco Bonacci, Brato Chakrabarti, David Saintillan, Olivia du Roure, Anke Lindner
arxiv-2205-08361.description: Abstract The fluid-structure interactions between flexible fibers and viscous flows play an essential role in various biological phenomena, medical problems, and industrial processes. Of particular interest is the case of particles freely transported in time-dependent flows. This work elucidates the dynamics and morphologies of actin filaments under oscillatory shear flows by combining microfluidic experiments, numerical simulations, and theoretical modeling.

arxiv-2210-06592.title: Can Calibration Improve Sample Prioritization?
arxiv-2210-06592.creator: Ganesh Tata, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Gopinath Chennupati, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan
arxiv-2210-06592.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Ganesh Tata, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Gopinath Chennupati, Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan. Calibration can reduce overconfident predictions of deep neural networks, but can calibration also accelerate training? In this paper, we show that it can when used to prioritize some examples for performing subset selection.

We provide an explicit example in degree 7 of such a foliation, in the non dicritical case, having a divergent separatrix, and subsequently, we study different families of such foliations in low degree. 1.

arxiv-2403-02994.title: SLICK: Strong Lensing Identification of Candidates Kindred in gravitational wave data
arxiv-2403-02994.creator: Sourabh Magare, Anupreeta More, Sunil Choudary
arxiv-2403-02994.description: Abstract By the end of the next decade, we hope to have detected strongly lensed gravitational waves by galaxies or clusters. Although there exist optimal methods for identifying lensed signal, it is shown that machine learning (ML) algorithms can give comparable performance but are orders of magnitude faster than non-ML methods.

arxiv-2403-20118.title: Balmer Decrement Anomalies in Galaxies at z ∼ 6 z\sim 6 Found by JWST Observations: Density-Bounded Nebulae or Excited H i Clouds?
arxiv-2403-20118.creator: Hiroto Yanagisawa, Masami Ouchi, Kimihiko Nakajima, Hidenobu Yajima, Hiroya Umeda, Shunsuke Baba, Takao Nakagawa, Minami Nakane, Akinori Matsumoto, Yoshiaki Ono, Yuichi Harikane, Yuki Isobe, Yi Xu, Yechi Zhang
arxiv-2403-20118.description: Abstract We investigate the physical origins of the Balmer decrement anomalies in GS-NDG-9422 (Cameron et al. 2023) and RXCJ2248-ID (Topping et al. 2024) galaxies at z ∼ 6 z\sim 6 whose H ​ α / H ​ β \mathrm{H}\alpha/\mathrm{H}\beta values are significantly smaller than 2.7 2.

arxiv-2410-03412.title: Team MTS @ AutoMin 2021: An Overview of Existing Summarization Approaches and Comparison to Unsupervised Summarization Techniques
arxiv-2410-03412.creator: Olga Iakovenko, Anna Andreeva, Anna Lapidus, Liana Mikaelyan
arxiv-2410-03412.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Olga Iakovenko, Anna Andreeva, Anna Lapidus, Liana Mikaelyan. Remote communication through video or audio conferences has become more popular than ever because of the worldwide pandemic. These events, therefore, have provoked the development of systems for automatic minuting of spoken language leading to AutoMin 2021 challenge. The following paper illustrates the results of the research that team MTS has carried out while participating in the Automatic Minutes challenge.

arxiv-2411-01396.title: Exploring the Edges of Latent State Clusters for Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2411-01396.creator: Yuanlin Duan, Guofeng Cui, He Zhu
arxiv-2411-01396.description: Abstract Exploring unknown environments efficiently is a fundamental challenge in unsupervised goal-conditioned reinforcement learning. While selecting exploratory goals at the frontier of previously explored states is an effective strategy, the policy during training may still have limited capability of reaching rare goals on the frontier, resulting in reduced exploratory behavior.

arxiv-2504-06570.title: Predicting data value before collection: A coefficient for prioritizing sources under random distribution shift
arxiv-2504-06570.creator: Ivy Zhang, Dominik Rothenhäusler
arxiv-2504-06570.description: Abstract Researchers often face choices between multiple data sources that differ in quality, cost, and representativeness. Which sources will most improve predictive performance? We study this data prioritization problem under a random distribution shift model, where candidate sources arise from random perturbations to a target population.

arxiv-2505-23938.title: Digital Forensic Investigation of the ChatGPT Windows Application
arxiv-2505-23938.creator: Malithi Wanniarachchi Kankanamge, Nick McKenna, Santiago Carmona, Syed Mhamudul Hasan, Abdur R. Shahid, Ahmed Imteaj
arxiv-2505-23938.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Malithi Wanniarachchi Kankanamge, Nick McKenna, Santiago Carmona, Syed Mhamudul Hasan, Abdur R. Shahid, Ahmed Imteaj. The ChatGPT Windows application offers better user interaction in the Windows operating system (OS) by enhancing productivity and streamlining the workflow of ChatGPT’s utilization. However, there are potential misuses associated with this application that require rigorous forensic analysis. This study presents a holistic forensic analysis of the ChatGPT Windows application, focusing on identifying and recovering digital artifacts for investigative purposes.

arxiv-2510-07989.title: A Stable, Accurate and Well-Conditioned Time-Domain PMCHWT Formulation
arxiv-2510-07989.creator: Van Chien Le, Cedric Münger, Francesco P. Andriulli, and Kristof Cools
arxiv-2510-07989.description: Abstract This paper introduces a new boundary element formulation for transient electromagnetic scattering by homogeneous dielectric objects based on the time-domain PMCHWT equation. To address dense-mesh breakdown, a multiplicative Calderón preconditioner utilizing a modified static electric field integral operator is employed.

arxiv-2511-16209.title: PSM: Prompt Sensitivity Minimization via LLM-Guided Black-Box Optimization
arxiv-2511-16209.creator: Hussein Jawad, Nicolas J-B. Brunel
arxiv-2511-16209.description: Abstract System prompts are critical for guiding the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet they often contain proprietary logic or sensitive information, making them a prime target for extraction attacks. Adversarial queries can successfully elicit these hidden instructions, posing significant security and privacy risks.

arxiv-2601-17884.title: Nonperturbative double copy: worldline instantons, color thermality, and backreaction
arxiv-2601-17884.creator: John Joseph M. Carrasco, Yaxi Chen, Nicolas H. Pavao, Aslan Seifi
arxiv-2601-17884.description: Abstract We present a first-principles, non-perturbative worldline instanton analysis of vacuum decay in the non-abelian Yang-Mills root of a Schwarzschild background. We recover the gauge theory color-thermal spectrum as a topological winding mode. The double copy maps vacuum response from the gauge theory directly to the gravity theory.

Originally considered as purely non-functional glue for neurons, decades of research have highlighted the importance

pmc-10566291.title: Gut microbiota interacts with inflammatory responses in acute pancreatitis
pmc-10566291.creator: Linjun Wu, Jing Hu, Xiaolin Yi, Jianqin Lv, Jiaqi Yao, Wenfu Tang, Shu Zhang, Meihua Wan
pmc-10566291.description: Acute pancreatitis (AP) is one of the most common acute abdominal conditions, and its incidence has been increasing for years. Approximately 15–20% of patients develop severe AP (SAP), which is complicated by critical inflammatory injury and intestinal dysfunction. AP-associated inflammation can lead to the gut barrier and function damage, causing dysbacteriosis and facilitating intestinal microbiota migration.

pmc-11311922.title: Characterization of a novel multi-resistant Pseudomonas juntendi strain from China with chromosomal blaVIM−2 and a megaplasmid coharboring blaIMP−1−like and blaOXA−1
pmc-11311922.creator: Shiman Jiang, Yaling Li, Kefan Bi, Sisi Yang, He Xia, Shengjie Li, Hui Chen, Lanjuan Li
pmc-11311922.description: BackgroundPseudomonas juntendi is a newly identified opportunistic pathogen, of which we have limited understanding. P. juntendi strains are often multidrug resistant, which complicates clinical management of infection.MethodsA strain of Pseudomonas juntendi (strain L4326) isolated from feces was characterized by MALDI-TOF-MS and Average Nucleotide Identity BLAST. This strain was further subject to whole-genome sequencing and Maximum Likelihood phylogenetic analysis.

pmc-11526131.title: Adaptive fuzzy neural super-twisting control of micro gyroscope sensor
pmc-11526131.creator: Jiapeng Xie, Juntao Fei
pmc-11526131.description: To maintain the vibrations of the gyroscope proof mass, an adaptive super-twisting sliding mode control (STSMC) of a micro gyroscope based on a two-loop recursive fuzzy neural network (TLRFNN) is designed. In order to estimate the unknown parameters of the nonlinear system online, an adaptive technology is adopted based on the parameter linearization of the nonlinear model.

pmc-11626031.title: Construction and Characterization of a Full-Length Infectious cDNA Clone of a Strain of Watermelon Mosaic Virus Isolated from Melon
pmc-11626031.creator: Hae-Ryun Kwak, Su-bin Hong, Jeong-Eun Kim, Hee-Seong Byun, Bong-Choon Lee, Hong-Soo Choi, Mikyeong Kim
pmc-11626031.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Watermelon mosaic virus (WMV), a member of the genus Potyvirus, causes serious economic losses in cucurbit crops. For molecular biological studies of viruses, it is necessary to construct an infectious clone that can facilitate gene functional analysis. In this study, we constructed an infectious cDNA clone of WMV genomic RNA by Gibson assembly and evaluated its virulence and symptoms on a variety of host plants.

pmc-11713814.title: Tau Magnitude and eXent–Tau‐MaX: Capturing tau spread and local accumulation provides a robust metric of tau burden
pmc-11713814.creator: Christopher Brown, Sandhitsu R Das, Katheryn A Q Cousins, Thomas F Tropea, Alice Chen‐Plotkin, Eddie B Lee, Ilya M Nasrallah, John A Detre, Paul A Yushkevich, Leslie M Shaw, David A Wolk
pmc-11713814.description: BackgroundMeasures of tau burden have typically relied upon measures of magnitude, such as mean standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR), or extent, such as number of tau positive regions. However, heterogenous patterns of tau spread and accumulation present challenges to using these measures in isolation to quantify tau burden.

pmc-12596939.title: Health insurance literacy and the associated factors in Iran: A national-scale study
pmc-12596939.creator: Zahra Asadi-Piri, Foroozan Abdollahi-pour, Namam Ali Azadi, Rajabali Daroudi, Ebrahim Jaafaripooyan
pmc-12596939.description: Highlights•National survey shows moderate Health Insurance Literacy score.•HIL varies significantly by gender,age, education, job, and income.•Men, older adults, and highly educated groups report higher HIL levels.•Some less-developed provinces outperform urban areas in HIL scores.•Findings call for targeted, equity-focused HIL education interventions.

pmc-12679267.title: Unravelling the reversion mechanisms of activated hepatic stellate cell properties by extracellular vesicles from mesenchymal stem cells
pmc-12679267.creator: Md Ariful Islam, Jannatul Mawya, Umme Salma, Noor Hayaty Abu Kasim, Nazmul Haque
pmc-12679267.description: Hepatic fibrosis is a pathological process characterized by an imbalance between the deposition and degradation of extracellular matrix components. This process is initiated by chronic liver injuries resulting from viral infections, alcoholic liver disease, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and autoimmune-mediated hepatic damage. If left untreated, hepatic fibrosis can progress to life-threatening conditions such as cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma.

pmc-13054052.title: Quantity and quality of antibiotic use in surgical and medical wards in a general academic hospital: A retrospective study
pmc-13054052.creator: Mariyatul Qibtiyah, Afini Safiro, Agustina Damayanti, Musofa Rusli, Harry Parathon, Usman Hadi, Kuntaman Kuntaman, Joni Wahyuhadi, Junaidi Khotib
pmc-13054052.description: Treatment of infectious diseases uses antibiotics to kill or inhibit the growth of pathogenic bacteria. Inappropriate antibiotic use triggers resistance, which in turn affects patient clinical outcomes, length of hospital stays, and treatment costs. This study aimed to analyze trends in the quantity and quality of antibiotics used in surgical and medical wards. This study was conducted at the Dr.

pmc-13540586.title: The Quantitative Analysis of Patients’ Dignity and Privacy Needs in Anesthesia Nursing Services Based on the Kano and SERVQUAL Models
pmc-13540586.creator: Yan Cao, Huqing Liu, Xiaolan Feng
pmc-13540586.description: BackgroundPatients undergoing pulmonary anesthesia face dignity and privacy threats due to intraoperative positioning, unconsciousness, and postoperative discomfort. Existing studies focus mainly on technical safety, lacking systematic investigation from the patient’s perspective. This neglect may lead to patient dissatisfaction and ethical concerns.
